default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vi: I played tennis with my older brother.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle と shows the person who joins in performing the action.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the direct object affected by the action of playing.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The main predicate is in the polite past form and describes a completed action.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.why: This sentence describes a past action with all its parts: the person acting together (N と), the action content (N を), and the sentence-ending predicate.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Using に means moving toward one receiving side, rather than showing two-way participation together as と does.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q1.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the reading of 兄 (あに - used when talking about their own older brother) with お兄さん (おにいさん - when calling or talking about someone else’s older brother).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject performing the action in a sentence describing a directly observed event.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb はしる changes to the て form to connect with the auxiliary verb showing the direction of movement.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern V-てくる describes movement toward the speaker’s location.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.why: The subject takes the particle が to report a scene happening before the speaker’s eyes, combined with the pattern V-てきました to show movement toward the observer.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It describes movement getting farther from the speaker’s location (running away), rather than running closer.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q2.kobun.tip: Pay attention to the difference between the directions of V-てくる (moving closer to the speaker) and V-ていく (moving away from the speaker).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.vi: There is an old loaf of bread in the refrigerator.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に shows the place where an object exists.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.1.vi: old / kept for a long time
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The い-ending adjective directly modifies the noun パン that follows it.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject that is present in a state.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The intransitive verb 入る changes to the て form to combine with います, showing a resulting state.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern V-ています combines with an intransitive verb to describe a state that continues to exist.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.why: This sentence describes the static state of an object with an intransitive verb (入る + ています). The location takes に, and the existing object takes が.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Using the transitive verb (is putting in) emphasizes a person’s intentional action instead of the object’s existing state.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q3.kobun.tip: Distinguish the intransitive verb 入る (go inside / be inside -> 入っている) from the transitive verb 入れる (put in -> 入れている).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は moves the object to the beginning of the sentence as the main topic.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: This relative time word acts as an adverb and modifies the verb without needing the particle に.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The main predicate is in the polite past form and describes acquiring knowledge or a skill.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.why: The object “this” is made the topic of the sentence with the particle は, followed by the time and the completed past action.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Using を gives the feeling of simply reporting a usual action, without highlighting the object as the topic of discussion as は does.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q4.kobun.tip: Relative time words such as きのう, きょう, and あした are not used with the particle に.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vi: I bought a pair of black shoes.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The い-ending adjective comes before a noun and directly describes its color.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object that was bought.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The main predicate is in the polite past form and shows a completed action.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.why: The い-ending adjective directly modifies the noun to form a complete object phrase, which then combines with the particle を and the past-tense verb.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: The noun 黒 + the particle の can also modify the noun in a similar way, but it focuses more on color classification than on direct visual description.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q5.kobun.tip: Do not add the particle の after the い-ending adjective when it directly modifies a noun (do not use 黒いのくつ).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vi: What time do you usually go to bed?
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The frequency adverb comes at the beginning of the sentence and modifies a daily habit.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The suffix ごろ attaches to a time expression to ask about an approximate time.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The polite verb combines with the question particle か at the end of the sentence to form a question.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q6.kobun.why: The frequency adverb identifies a habitual action. It combines with an expression asking for an approximate time (何時ごろ) and a polite question predicate.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: The particle に can be added after ごろ, but in everyday speech Japanese speakers often omit に.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q6.kobun.tip: Distinguish ごろ (an approximate point in time: 何時ごろ - around what time) from ぐらい (an approximate duration: 何時間ぐらい - about how many hours).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vi: I do not have an older sister.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に shows the owner of a family relationship in an existence sentence.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the object the topic and emphasizes the negative clause that follows.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb いる changes to the polite negative form いません to show that a person does not exist.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.why: The sentence expresses possession of a family relationship with the structure “N1 に N2 が/は います/いません.” Here, the particle は replaces が to emphasize the negative meaning “do not have.”
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Making “I” the main topic of the whole sentence with は and using が for “older sister” gives a similarly natural expression.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: This is grammatically incorrect because ありません is used only for lifeless objects, not for people.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse using ありません instead of いません when talking about family members.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q7.kobun.cn: N に + N が/は + います/いません
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に goes with a noun showing the state or result of a change.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb なる in the polite past form shows the natural change of time or the seasons.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.cn: N に・Aな に・Aい（remove い + く） + なります
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.why: The pattern “N に なります” describes a natural change in the weather or a state, without human intention causing it.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: The particle is incorrect because なる is an intransitive verb showing a natural change, so it does not take the object particle を.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: The verb する shows a person’s intentional choice instead of a natural change in the weather.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q8.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often mistakenly use the particle を because of the Vietnamese expression “welcome autumn/become autumn,” instead of using the particle に with なる.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vi: Everyone, let’s collect the trash together.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で comes after a word for a group of people to show the manner or scope of performing an action together.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the direct object affected by the action of collecting.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 集める changes to the て form to combine with the auxiliary verb ください that follows.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: It comes after a verb in the て form to create a polite request.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.why: The sentence gives a group request with the manner “みんなで,” targeting the object affected “ごみを,” and ending with the polite request pattern “Vてください.”
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: Change it from a request into a statement describing an action in progress (everyone is collecting the trash together).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: Change it into a prohibition that strictly forbids the action (do not collect the trash).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t1-q9.kobun.tip: Distinguish the transitive verb 集める (changed to 集めて) from the intransitive verb 集まる (changed to 集まって) when used with the particle を.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: This high-frequency adverb directly modifies the action of drinking alcohol.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object receiving the action of drinking.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb のむ changes to the polite form ます to describe a daily action or habit.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The question particle is placed at the end of the sentence to form a question for the listener.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.why: The frequency adverb よく comes first and modifies the whole action phrase “drink alcohol.” It combines with the question particle か at the end to ask about a daily habit.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Change to the adverb あまり with the negative ending ません to ask for confirmation about a habit that happens rarely (Don’t you drink alcohol very often?).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: Change to the ending たい です to ask about the desire to drink alcohol instead of asking about an actual habit.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q1.kobun.tip: Frequency adverbs such as よく come before the object phrase or the verb. Do not add a particle after よく.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vi: I want to meet my parents.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.sk: N と + N に + Vます（remove ます）たい です
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle と links nouns referring to people as equals.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the direct recipient of the action of meeting.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 会う omits ます and adds たい to express the speaker's wishes and hopes.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: It comes after the adjective ending たい to make the sentence more formal and polite.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.cn: Vます（remove ます） + たい（です）
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.why: The nouns 父 and 母 are listed with the particle と, followed by the particle に to show the target of the verb 会う, and ending with the structure 〜たい です, which expresses the speaker's wish.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: The particle is wrong because the object of the verb 会う must use に, not を.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: The pattern 〜たがっている describes another person's wish. It is not used for the speaker's own direct wish.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q2.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the particle を with に before the verb 会う (to meet someone).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies the main subject being described and evaluated.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: A high-degree adverb that directly modifies the adjective ひろい that follows.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending in い acts as the predicate describing a feature. It combines with です to form a polite expression.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.why: This sentence describes a characteristic of something in the basic order: 'Topic (は) + degree adverb (とても) + adjective predicate (ひろいです)'.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Change the predicate to the negative form 'not very wide' (usually combined with the adverb あまり rather than とても).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: Change it to the past tense to report a past impression of the sea (the sea was very wide).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q3.kobun.tip: When changing an adjective ending in い into the polite form by adding です, always keep the ending い. Do not remove the ending い.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を identifies the window as the object affected by the action of opening.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb in the て form combines with も to create a concessive condition for asking permission.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: This ending is used to politely ask the other person for permission.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.why: This sentence uses the permission pattern 「～てもいいですか」. The object 「まど」 uses the particle 「を」 with the transitive verb 「あける」 in the て form.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence becomes a prohibition: 'You must not open the window'.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used, the sentence expresses an obligation: 'You must open the window'.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the particle が with を before the verb in the pattern ～てもいいですか when asking permission to do something.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q4.kobun.cn: Vて + もいい（です/ですか）
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vi: While waiting, I sat and read a magazine.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: A clause modifying the noun あいだ describes a continuous period of time.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を identifies the magazine as the direct object of reading.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The predicate is in the past progressive tense to show that the action continued throughout the waiting period.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.why: The pattern 「あいだ」 follows the clause 「待っている」 to create a time frame that continues for a period. The second clause uses the progressive form 「読んでいました」 to show that the action continued throughout that entire period.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「あいだに」 is used, the second clause must describe a short action that happens at a specific moment, not an action that continues.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If 「うちに」 is used, the sentence suggests doing something while there is still time, before the situation changes.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often confuse 「あいだ」（the latter action continues in parallel） with 「あいだに」（the latter action happens immediately, in a short moment）.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q5.kobun.cn: V辞書形/Vている/Vない・Aい・Aな・Nの + あいだ（に）
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vi: Around what time do you usually wake up?
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: A frequency adverb that modifies the predicate verb to ask about daily habits.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: A word used to ask about a point in time, combined with the approximate suffix ごろ to indicate an approximate time.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The predicate in the polite form ます combines with the question particle か to form a question.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.why: A question about a daily habit, with the frequency adverb 「いつも」 at the beginning. The time point uses 「何時」 with the approximate suffix 「ごろ」 and ends with the polite form 「～ますか」.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If the particle 「に」 is added, the sentence is still grammatically correct, but in natural conversation people usually omit 「に」 after 「ごろ」.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If 「くらい」 is used, it asks about the length of a period (how many hours someone sleeps), not the time when someone wakes up.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t2-q6.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse 「ごろ」（, used for a point in time, such as around what time）, with 「ぐらい/くらい」（, used for the length of a period, such as approximately how long）.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vi: Please boil the water for me.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を shows that the water is the object affected by boiling.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The transitive verb is put into the て form so that it can connect directly to the request pattern ください.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: This sentence ending is used to make a polite request or ask the other person for help.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.why: This sentence uses the polite request pattern 「～てください」. The noun 「おゆ」 is the direct object of the transitive verb 「わかす」 in the て form.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used, the request sounds more polite and shows a higher level of respect for the other person.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern replaces it, the sentence becomes a prohibition: 'You must not boil the water'.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q1.kobun.tip: Be careful to distinguish the intransitive verb 「わく」（, meaning that the water boils by itself, which uses が）, from the transitive verb 「わかす」（, meaning to boil water, which uses を）, so that you do not use the wrong particle.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vi: The concert is held at the church.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.sk: N(place) で + N(event) が + V受身
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle で indicates the place where an event takes place.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject affected in a passive sentence.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb ひらく is changed to the passive form to show that the event is held.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.cn: A Group 1 verb changes its u-ending to are + ます
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.why: The sentence uses the passive form ひらかれます to describe the event objectively as something that is held. The particle で indicates the place where the event takes place.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: Change it to the active form, meaning that someone opens or organizes it.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q10.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the particle に with で when indicating the place where an event is held.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vi: As for sports, I prefer watching them to playing them myself.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes sports the main topic of the comparison.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle で indicates the manner or the person directly performing the action.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern よりも follows a dictionary-form verb to set the activity being placed second in the comparison.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies the noun ほう to form the action that is chosen.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The noun ほう combines with the particle が to serve as the subject of the following adjective expressing preference.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: The adjective ending in な acts as the predicate expressing preference for the chosen option.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.cn: V辞書形/N + より（も） + V辞書形/N（の） + ほうが + adjective
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.why: The sentence uses a comparative structure between two actions: 「A より B のほうが...」. The topic 「スポーツ」 comes first with the particle 「は」. Both actions 「する」 and 「見る」 are in the dictionary form to compare preference.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: When directly comparing two nouns, the particle の must be added before ほう (for example: テニスより サッカーの ほうが すきです).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If the less-than comparison pattern 「するほど すきではない」 is used, it means 'I do not like it as much as playing it myself'.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q2.kobun.tip: When comparing two actions, the verb before ほう must stay in the dictionary form. Do not add の (avoid mistakenly saying *見るのほうが).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vi: Yesterday, I had a meal at a restaurant with Mr. Yamakawa.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.sk: 時 + N（person） と + N（place） で + N を + Vました
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: A word for past time that acts as an adverb to identify when an event happened.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle と indicates someone who participates in the action together with the subject.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で indicates the place where the action of eating takes place.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を combines with the noun しょくじ to form the object of the verb しました.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb is in the polite past tense, showing that the action was completed.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.why: This basic statement gives a sequence of information about an action in the past. The adverb 「きのう」 establishes the time, the person acting together with the subject uses 「と」, the place of the action uses 「で」, and the predicate ends in the past tense 「しました」.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 「に」 is incorrect because 「で」 is the particle for the place where an action occurs, while 「に」 is used only for a place of existence or a destination.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If 「へ」 or 「に」 is used, the predicate must change to a movement verb such as 「行きました」.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q3.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the particle 「で」（, which indicates the place where an action occurs）, with 「に」（, which indicates a place of existence or a destination for movement.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vi: Please polish the window glass until it is clean and shiny.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The direct object marked by particle を is the object affected by the cleaning action.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending in な changes to に to form an adverb of result or state that modifies the verb みがく.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The main verb takes the て form and combines with particle ください to form a request.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: A sentence-ending grammar pattern used to make a polite request.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.why: The sentence follows the polite request structure '〜てください'. The adverb 'きれいに' is placed directly before the verb to show the desired result after polishing the glass.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence becomes more polite and formal when asking someone for a favor.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If this pattern is used instead, the sentence becomes negative and means 'please do not polish it'.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q4.kobun.tip: Learners often forget to change the adjective ending in な to に when it modifies a verb. They may incorrectly write きれい みがいて.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vi: After lunch, I usually drink two cups of coffee.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: A noun with particle の modifies the noun showing the time 後で.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The noun phrase + で shows the point in time when the next action takes place.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The direct object affected by the action of drinking is marked by particle を.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The counter showing the quantity comes directly before the verb and modifies the action.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The main predicate takes the polite ます form to express a habit.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.why: The sentence sets a time when one event is completed first (ひるごはんの 後で), then states a habitual action with a counter (２はい) placed directly before the predicate.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If 'ひるごはんを たべてから' is used, the sentence emphasizes the fixed order of the actions, which cannot be reversed.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If 'ひるごはんの まえに' is used instead, the meaning is reversed to 'before lunch'.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q5.kobun.tip: When combining a noun with 後で, learners often forget particle の between them. They may incorrectly say ひるごはん 後で.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vi: Because the exam is coming soon, I am taking careful notes diligently.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The subject of the subordinate clause showing the reason, used with particle が.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending in い combines with conjunction ので to explain an objective reason.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb showing the manner and attitude used when taking notes.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The object combines with particle を to form the fixed verb phrase ノートをとる (to take notes).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb とる takes the て form to combine with the auxiliary verb います.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: An auxiliary verb showing a habit or an action that is being maintained regularly.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.why: The objective-reason subordinate clause 'ので' comes at the beginning as the basis for the regular action currently being performed in the main clause (〜ています).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 'ちかいから' is used, the reason sounds more subjective and emphasizes personal feelings more than 'ので'.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If 'ちかいのに' is used instead, the sentence becomes a contrast with a blaming or surprised tone (even though the exam is almost here...).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.tip: When using ので with a noun or an adjective ending in な, learners often mistakenly use だ instead of な. For example, they may say しけんだので instead of しけんなので.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな（な）・Nな + ので
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vi: I plan to ask someone to buy clothes for me at the department store.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle で marks the place where the shopping action takes place.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The direct object of the action of buying, marked by particle を.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb takes the て form to combine with the receiving-and-giving verb もらう.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The receiving-and-giving verb shows that the speaker receives help from another person.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: A sentence-ending pattern showing the speaker's fixed intention or plan.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.why: The sentence combines the receiving-and-giving structure '〜てもらう' (asking someone to do something) with the intention pattern '〜つもりです' to express a plan to receive help from another person.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is changed to 'かって あげる つもりです', the direction of the action is reversed and means 'I plan to buy clothes for someone'.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If 'かって くれる' is used, the subject must be another person who performs the action. It cannot be used directly with the speaker's own 'つもりです'.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the direction of the action between '〜てもらう' (I receive an action from someone else) and '〜てあげる' (I do something for someone else).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q7.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 + つもりだ / つもりです; Vて + もらう
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vi: The supermarket in front of the station has very cheap food.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The noun phrase + の gives the location of the supermarket noun (スーパー).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The main topic of the whole sentence is marked by particle は.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The smaller subject of the adjective: the specific thing whose characteristic is described by particle が.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending in い serves as the main predicate and describes a characteristic.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.why: The sentence uses the description pattern 'A は B が adjective'. A is the whole thing made the topic (えき前のスーパーは), while B is the specific part or attribute being evaluated (しょくりょうひんが やすいです).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 'しょくりょうひんも やすいです' is used instead, the sentence also implies that 'the food is cheap too, along with other items'.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If 'しょくりょうひんは やすいです' is used, the sentence has a contrastive tone: only the food is cheap, while the other items may not be.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q8.kobun.tip: In the structure 'A は B が adjective', learners often use は in both positions or switch the positions of は and が.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vi: I will work part-time, then use the money I receive to go abroad.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The object with particle を combines with verb して to form the action of working part-time.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb takes the て form with a comma to connect the sequence of actions that happens first.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The past-tense verb acts as a relative clause that directly modifies the noun お金.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: Particle で shows the means or financial source used to carry out the next action.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: Particle へ shows the direction or destination of the movement.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: The main predicate is in the polite form and describes movement in the future.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.cn: Vた + N (a relative clause modifying a noun)
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.why: The sentence uses the て form to connect actions in time (work part-time -> earn money). It also uses the relative clause 'もらった お金' as the financial means (で) for the goal of going abroad.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If '外国に 行きます' is used, the sentence emphasizes a specific destination more than the general direction of movement in 'へ'.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If 'お金で' is changed to 'お金から', the sentence means taking money from a source, rather than using all the money as the means of payment.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t3-q9.kobun.tip: Learners often forget the order of a relative clause in Japanese. They may incorrectly say お金 もらった because of Vietnamese grammar habits.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vi: I went to my aunt's house.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q1.kobun.sk: N1 の + N2 (place) へ + V (movement)
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: Particle の connects a noun showing ownership or relationship and modifies noun うち.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: Particle へ shows the direction and destination of movement.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The main predicate is in the polite past tense.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q1.kobun.why: The noun phrase おばのうち serves as the destination and combines with particle へ to modify the movement verb いきました.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Particle に also shows a destination, but it emphasizes reaching the destination rather than the direction of movement.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q1.kobun.tip: When particle へ shows direction, it is pronounced e, not he.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the person who is known.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The honorific form of しっていますか, used to ask the listener politely.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q2.kobun.why: This question uses the honorific form ごぞんじですか to show respect to the listener when asking whether they know a person or thing.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: A usual polite expression that does not show a high level of respect toward the listener.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q2.kobun.tip: Do not use ごぞんじです when talking about yourself. Use しっています or ぞんじております instead.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q2.kobun.cn: N を + ごぞんじだ
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.sk: Time + N (higher-ranking person) に + おめにかかりました
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: A past-time adverb that identifies when an action happened.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the person who receives the action of meeting.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: A component of the humble expression おめにかかる.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: A polite past-tense verb that completes the humble expression おめにかかる.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.why: Use the special humble expression おめにかかる instead of あう to lower yourself when meeting someone of higher status, such as a director.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: The general humble form, with the same meaning but a somewhat different level of formality.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use おめにかかる to describe another person's action of meeting you.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q3.kobun.cn: N に + おめにかかる
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vi: Mr. Smith is teaching English to Mr. Tanaka.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the subject as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the person who receives the knowledge from the action of teaching.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the direct content being taught.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb おしえる takes the て form to combine with the progressive auxiliary verb.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern ています shows that work or an action is in progress.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.why: This structure describes who teaches what to whom. It combines with the ています form to show an ongoing job or activity.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It means learning from someone, so the roles of the giver and receiver of knowledge are reversed.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q4.kobun.tip: Do not confuse the subject and the person marked by the particle に in the two verbs おしえる and ならう.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The verb あやまる takes the continuative form to connect with the polite auxiliary verb.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: A sentence-ending auxiliary verb for the polite form.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q5.kobun.why: A simple sentence with a polite predicate that expresses the action of apologizing in the future.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: The past tense shows that the apology has already been made.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t4-q5.kobun.tip: The verb あやまる belongs to group 1, so its final ru changes to ri in the masu form.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t5-q1.tokens.0.m: besides; except for / unexpectedly; beyond expectations
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vi: A: "Teacher, may I write with a ballpoint pen?" - B: "No, please write with a pencil."
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: A form of address placed at the beginning of a sentence to call the listener before asking a question.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle 「で」 shows the means or tool used to write.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb takes the 「〜ても」 form and combines with 「いいですか」 to make a permission question.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: A sentence-final grammar pattern used to ask the other person politely for permission.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: A short and polite negative reply.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle 「で」 shows the means or tool that is requested.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: A predicate using the pattern 「〜てください」 to give a polite request or instruction.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.why: The speaker uses the permission structure 「〜てもいいですか」 with the particle 「で」 for the tool, and the respondent gives an alternative instruction using the pattern 「〜てください」.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If B uses 「〜てはいけません」, it sounds like a strict prohibition and is less common in ordinary instructional conversation.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.tip: When asking permission to do something with a particular tool, always use the particle 「で」 before 「 Vてもいいですか」 instead of the particle 「を」.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q1.kobun.cn: Vて + もいいですか / Vて + ください
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vi:
A:「What is global warming?」
B:「It is the temperature around the world continuing to rise.」
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: Marks the person asking the question.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle って is used in casual speech instead of は or というのは to introduce the concept that needs to be defined.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: The question word なん combines with ですか to ask for an explanation.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: Marks the person giving the explanation.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle で, together with the suffix 中, shows the area where the natural phenomenon occurs.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle が marks the subject of the natural phenomenon in the modifying clause.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.6.n: The pattern V-ていく shows a continuing change moving toward the future. It modifies the noun こと.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.ch.7.n: The structure 〜ことだ is used to define a concept. It combines with the particle よ to emphasize the explanation.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.why: To explain a natural phenomenon that is increasing now and will continue to increase in the future, the sentence uses the pattern V-ていく, which shows a continuing change from the present onward, together with nominalization using ことだ.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: If 上がってきたこと is used, it describes a trend that has gradually increased from the past to the present, without emphasizing the future direction.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.vs.1.d: If only 上がること is used, it simply states a general fact and loses the sense of a gradual continuing change.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q10.kobun.tip: Remember: V-ていく describes an event or state that continues to develop from the present toward the future, moving farther away from the speaker.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vi:
A:「Mr. Tanaka, what is that?」
B:「This one? It is a doll. It is made of wood and paper.」
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: Calling the other person's name to begin the conversation.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: A demonstrative pronoun used as the topic of the conversation, with the particle は omitted.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: An interrogative predicate used to ask what an object is called.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: A question confirming the object being held.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: A noun predicate that introduces the name of the object.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle と connects nouns in a list that indicate materials.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.7.n: The particle で indicates a visible physical material that makes up a product.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.ch.8.n: The verb in the passive form 作られる combines with ています to describe the state of an item being made.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.why: Because the subject is an inanimate object (the doll), the verb uses the passive form 作られています; also, wood and paper are materials that can be seen directly, so they are used with the particle で.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 木と紙から作られます is wrong because から is used only for ingredients that have changed and no longer keep their original form (such as alcohol made from rice).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q11.kobun.tip: Distinguish clearly: N で 作る (a material clearly visible to the eye) and N から 作る (an ingredient processed so that its properties have changed).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.vi:
A:「Oh, what happened? You are completely wet.」
B:「I got caught in the rain because I did not bring an umbrella.」
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: An interjection commonly used by women to show surprise.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: A familiar question asking about someone's situation, ending with the particle の.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb showing that the wetness is beyond the normal level.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb in the て form is left unfinished at the end of the sentence to comment on the condition visible at that moment.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.5.vi: because of the rain; caught in the rain
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle に indicates a natural cause of trouble in the passive form showing harm.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.6.vi: I got caught in the rain.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.6.n: The intransitive verb uses the passive form showing harm (迷惑受身) to express the trouble and wetness caused by falling rain.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.7.n: The particle を marks the object of the action of carrying.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.8.n: The verb in the て form is used with the auxiliary verb いる to express a state of having something.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.9.vi: because I did not have one.」
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.ch.9.n: The past negative form combines with the conjunction ので to explain the reason for getting caught in the rain.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.cn: Intransitive verb (雨が降る) ＋ れる / られる (indirect passive / passive showing harm)
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.why: Speaker B uses the passive form showing harm (雨に降られる) to express the trouble and harm caused by a rain shower, and then uses the clause ので to explain why no umbrella was prepared.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 雨がふりました only gives the objective statement that it rained; it does not express the speaker's complaint or personal trouble.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q12.kobun.tip: When a natural phenomenon is put into the passive form (such as 雨に降られる and 雪に降られる), it always implies that the speaker has to suffer inconvenience or trouble.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.vi:
A:「I'm home.」
B:「You came home very late. Don't make Mom worry so much.」
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: A fixed greeting said when someone has just arrived home.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: An adverb showing that the time is much later than expected.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The past form of the い adjective combines with the modal particles わ and ね to express a mild but familiar complaint.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb used with the negative form to advise someone not to do something excessively.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: The negative causative form of the verb 〜させないで reminds the other person not to make the speaker worry.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.cn: V causative form ない (Vさせないで / Vないで)
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.why: Speaker B uses the causative form 心配させる (make someone worry) together with the reminding ending ないでね to ask speaker A not to come home late and make the family anxious again.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 心配しないでね means “Don't worry” (advising the other person not to worry), which is the complete opposite of “Don't make me worry.”
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q13.kobun.tip: Japanese learners often confuse 心配しないで (advising someone not to worry) with 心配させないで (reminding someone not to make the speaker worry).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vi:
A:「Every classroom is clean, isn't it?」 
 B:「This school makes the students clean them, you see.」
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative word is followed by the particle も to create an all-inclusive meaning.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.1.n: The noun combines with どの before it and も after it to mean that every classroom is included.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.2.n: The な-ending adjective serves as the predicate and combines with ですね to make a comment seeking agreement.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.3.n: The demonstrative word directly modifies the noun for school that follows.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle では both identifies the place where the action occurs and makes the place the topic.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle に marks the person required to perform the action in a causative sentence.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the cleaning action.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.7.vi: make them do it, you see.」
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.ch.7.n: The causative verb in the progressive form combines with から at the end of the sentence to explain the reason.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.cn: V使役 (Group 1: ending う→あ＋せる / Group 2: remove る＋させる / Group 3: する→させる, くる→こさせる) ＋ ている
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.why: Speaker B uses the causative form “させています” with the particle に after “学生” to show that the school requires the students to clean. The particle では emphasizes the scope of the school, and から at the end gives an explanation.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vs.0.d: Changing it to the request form would imply gratitude toward the students, rather than a school rule assigning the task.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.vs.1.d: It would simply describe the students cleaning by themselves and would not show direction or assignment by the school.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q14.kobun.tip: When the verb already has an object marked by を (such as そうじを), the person being made to act must use the particle に, not を.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.vi:
A:「Lee, that hat is beautiful!」 
 B:「This one? My older brother gave it to me.」
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.0.n: Calling the other person's name at the beginning of a conversation.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.1.n: The demonstrative word modifies the noun for hat that follows.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.2.n: It makes the object the topic to be commented on in a familiar statement.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.3.n: The な-ending adjective serves as the predicate and combines with ですね to give praise.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.4.n: A short question used to confirm the object that the other person has just praised.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle に indicates the person who gave the object to the speaker.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.ch.6.n: The past form of the giving-and-receiving verb indicates receiving an item from another person.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.cn: N (giver) に / から ＋ もらう / もらいました
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.why: Speaker B uses the verb “もらいました” with the particle “に” after “兄” to show that the older brother gave the hat to the speaker. In the conversation, the subject “I” and the object “the hat” are omitted because they are clear from the context.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.vs.0.d: This is wrong because あげました is used only when the subject is the speaker giving something to another person, not when another person gives something to the speaker.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.vs.1.d: The meaning is similar, but the viewpoint changes so that the older brother is the active subject who gives something to me.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q15.kobun.tip: Distinguish clearly: もらう uses the particle に for the giver (the subject is the receiver), while くれる uses the particle が for the giver.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vi:
A:「Excuse me, which direction is the station?」
B:「If you go straight, you will come out onto a main road, so please turn right there.」
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: A polite opening used to get someone's attention before asking for directions.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は marks “the station” as the main topic of the question.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The sentence ending でしょうか is used to ask for directions politely and formally.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb showing the manner of movement. It directly modifies the verb 行くと.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The V-ると pattern expresses a natural condition when giving directions: if you go in this direction, the following result will happen.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: An adjective ending in い modifies the noun 道 (path).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle に marks the destination or place where the action of going out (出ます) appears.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.7.n: The linking particle から gives the basis or reason for the next direction.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.8.n: The particle を is used with a movement verb to mark the space or place where one turns.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.9.n: The particle に shows the direction of the change in direction.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.10.n: The pattern 〜てください is used to give directions politely.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.why: When giving directions, Japanese speakers often use the natural conditional form「〜と」, together with the reason particle「〜から」, and end with an instruction「〜てください」. Note that the particle「を」is used for the place where you turn (そこを), while「に」is used for the direction of the turn (右に).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If you use 「行ったら」, the sentence is still grammatically correct, but 「〜と」 gives directions a more necessary and natural meaning in route-guidance conversations.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: Do not use 「そこで曲がる」 because in Japanese, a space or turning point that one moves through must take the particle 「を」.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.tip: Learners often mistakenly use the particles「で」or「に」instead of「を」before the place where they turn (it must be そこを曲がる, not そこに/そこで曲がる).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q2.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + と; Vて + ください
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vi:
A:「Kim, have you finished reading this book?」
B:「No, I have not read even one page yet.」
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.sk: もう + Vましたか + まだ + Number + も + Vていません
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: Calling the person's name to direct the listener's attention to the question.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The demonstrative この comes before and directly modifies the noun 本 that follows.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The object of the action of reading. The particle を is omitted in casual speech.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb showing that an action has been completed. It is used with a past-tense verb.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: A past-tense predicate used to ask whether an action has been completed.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: A negative word used to answer a confirmation question.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: An adverb showing that an action has not happened. It is always used with the negative ending 〜ていません.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.7.n: The structure “smallest number + も” is used with a negative form to emphasize complete negation.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.8.n: The pattern まだ〜ていません expresses that an action remains incomplete up to the present.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.cn: まだ + Vていません; Number + も + V (negative)
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.why: When giving a negative answer to a completion question「もう〜ましたか」, the required standard structure is「まだ〜ていません」. Add the smallest quantity「1ページ」together with the particle「も」to emphasize the absolute nature of the negation.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 「読みませんでした」 gives a simple past meaning (did not read at a certain time), so it does not express the state of not having read it up to the present.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: Using 「１ページは」 gives a contrastive meaning (read one page, but have not read the other pages), which is the complete opposite of the original meaning.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often translate “have not done” as the past tense, so they confuse it with「いいえ、読みませんでした」instead of saying「まだ読んでいません」.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vi:
A:「Yang, could you lend me your dictionary?」
B:「Sorry. I did not bring my dictionary today.」
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: An opening form of address used before making a request.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object being lent.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 貸す changes to the て form so it can combine with the auxiliary verb used for requests.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern 〜てくれませんか is used to ask someone to do something that benefits the speaker.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: An apology given before stating the reason for refusing a request.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: A time noun used as a time complement.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: The object of the action of bringing. The particle を is omitted in spoken language.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.7.vi: I did not bring it with me.」
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.7.n: The compound verb 持ってくる is changed to the past negative tense to explain that the item was not brought along.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.why: The speaker uses「〜てくれませんか」to ask the other person to perform an action (lend something). When refusing, the respondent uses the past tense「持ってきませんでした」to state that they did not prepare and bring it when they left.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It sounds more polite and humble than 「〜てくれませんか」.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: Used when the speaker offers to help the other person, unlike「〜てくれませんか」, which asks the other person to help the speaker.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q4.kobun.tip: Clearly distinguish「貸す」(lend—someone else does the action) from「借りる」(borrow—the speaker does the action). When asking someone to lend something, use「貸してください/貸してくれませんか」, not 借りる.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vi:
A:「It will soon be March, won't it?」
B:「The weather has become much warmer, hasn't it?」
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb showing that a time or event is about to arrive.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.1.vi:
it will be March soon, won't it? 
 B:「
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: A noun predicate combines with the modal particle ね to seek agreement.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb showing a clear degree of change in a state.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.3.vi: has gradually become warmer, hasn't it?」
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern A(い->く)なる combines with てくる to describe a continuing change of state from the past up to the present.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.why: To describe a change in the weather or a state that began earlier and has gradually continued up to the present, Japanese combines the state change「〜くなる」with the continuing direction「〜てくる」.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Describes a change that starts now and continues toward the future.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: It only reports that the weather has become warm and does not emphasize the gradual process of change as「〜てきました」does.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse「〜てくる」(a change moving toward the present) with「〜ていく」(a change continuing and developing toward the future).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q5.kobun.cn: Aい(く)・Aな(に)・N(に) ＋ なって ＋ くる
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vi:
A:「Lee is very late, isn't he?」
B:「That's true. Let's try waiting another 10 minutes and see what happens.」
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.sk: Aい ですねえ ＋ あと ＋ Number word ＋ Vて ＋ みましょう
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: Call the person mentioned in the conversation by name.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective 遅い combines with the exclamatory ending ですねえ to comment on the lateness.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: A filler phrase showing strong agreement with the other person's opinion.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb indicating the remaining amount of time or quantity, or an additional amount that is needed.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: A number phrase indicating the length of time that will continue to be spent waiting.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.5.vi: let's try waiting and see what happens.」
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern Vてみる (try doing something) combines with the inviting ending 〜ましょう to suggest trying to wait together and seeing the result.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ みる; V(remove ます) ＋ ましょう
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.why: The speaker uses 「あと」 with a number phrase to indicate an additional period of time, then combines the trial pattern 「〜てみる」 with the inviting ending 「〜ましょう」 to suggest trying an action and seeing how things develop.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: It simply means 'let's wait' and does not have the nuance of patiently trying to wait and see whether the person will arrive, as in 「待ってみましょう」.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: It asks the other person to wait; it is not a suggestion that both people do it together, as in 「〜ましょう」.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q6.kobun.tip: Remember that the pattern 「〜てみる」 means 'try doing something,' not the verb 'to look/see' in the original sense of 見る.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vi:
A:「What happened? I heard a loud noise coming from...」
B:「I'm sorry. I accidentally dropped the cup and broke it.」
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The pattern 〜んですか is used to ask for more details and find out the cause of something that has just happened.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The attributive word 大きな comes before and modifies the noun 音.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the source of the phenomenon perceived by the senses in the structure 音がする.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb する combines with the particle が to introduce the situation before asking the question.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: A sincere apology for causing the problem.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle を marks the direct object affected by the action of dropping.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.6.n: The transitive verb 落とす is put into form て to link the cause to the following result.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.7.n: The pattern 〜てしまう describes an action that was done accidentally and led to an regrettable, unintended result.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.cn: N が する (sound/taste/feeling); Vて ＋ しまう (accidentally do something / regret it)
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.why: The first part uses the sensory phrase 「音がする」 with 「が」 to introduce the question; the second part uses the linking form て to connect the cause and result (dropping it led to breaking it), and ends with 「〜てしまいました」 to show regret about the unintended accident.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: Using the intransitive verb only reports that the cup broke; it does not show the speaker's responsibility for accidentally dropping it or the regret expressed by 「割ってしまいました」.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: It is simply the past tense of the transitive verb describing the action of breaking something, and lacks the guilty, accidental nuance of 「〜てしまいました」.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q7.kobun.tip: You must distinguish the transitive verb 割る (break something—an intentional or unintentional human action) from the intransitive verb 割れる (break by itself); when you cause the problem yourself and apologize, you must use the transitive verb 「割ってしまいました」.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vi:
A:「Is that magazine interesting?」
B:「Yes. I have already finished reading it, so please take it if you would like.」
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: Marks the person who begins the question turn.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: A demonstrative word that directly modifies the following noun ざっし.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: A noun introduced as the topic of discussion (the particle は is omitted in speech).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending in い serves as the main predicate and combines with ですか to ask for an opinion politely.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: An affirmative reply that begins speaker B's answer.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: An adverb showing that an action was completed before the time of speaking.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.6.vi: because I have finished reading it,
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: The pattern V-てしまう describes the reading as fully completed and combines with から to state the reason.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.7.n: A polite conditional expression used when making a suggestion or offering something to the other person.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.8.n: An adverb used at the end of a line of dialogue to invite the listener to take or use something.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.why: Speaker B uses the pattern V-てしまいました with the adverb もう to emphasize that the magazine has been read completely, thereby giving a reasonable reason (から) for offering it to speaker A.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 読んでいます is used, it only describes the state of being partway through reading and does not show that the reading is finished so the magazine can be offered.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If only 読みました is used, it simply reports that the reading happened in the past and does not emphasize complete accomplishment.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.tip: Besides expressing regret, the pattern 〜てしまう also means that an action has been completed fully (often used with もう or すっかり).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q8.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ しまう / しまいました
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vi:
A:「What should I do with the book after I finish reading it?」
B:「Oh, please put it back on the shelf yourself.」
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: Marks the person who begins the conversation.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The past-tense verb modifies the following noun 本.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は makes the book that has been read the topic about which advice is requested.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The question word どう combines with the conditional form たら to set up a question asking for advice.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern 〜たらいいですか is used to ask for instructions or advice about what to do.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: An interjection used to receive the other person's question.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle で shows that the subject performs the action personally.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: The particle に indicates the destination or place where the item is returned.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.8.vi: please put it back ready for later use.」
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.8.n: The pattern V-ておく combines with ください to ask someone to return an item to its original place in preparation for its next use.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.why: When A uses the structure for asking how to handle something, 〜たらいいですか, B uses 〜ておいてください to instruct A to return the item to its original place so it is ready for future use.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If only もどしてください is used, it simply asks someone to return the book and lacks the meaning of leaving it ready for the next use.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If もどしてしまってください is used, it has the nuance of urging someone to finish putting the book away quickly.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.tip: In everyday communication, the pattern V-ておく is often used when returning an item to its original place after using it.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t6-q9.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ おく / おいてください
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vi: Mr. Tanaka married Ms. Lee's younger sister.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies Mr. Tanaka as the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の shows the family relationship modifying the noun meaning younger sister that follows.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle と indicates the person who participates in the reciprocal action of marriage.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: A past-tense verb showing that the event has actually been completed.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.cn: N(partner) ＋ と ＋ けっこんする
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.why: The verb 'けっこんする' (to marry) requires a mutual action by both sides, so the other person involved must be marked with the particle 'と'. The person performing the action is made the subject with the particle 'は'.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: The particle is incorrect because marriage is a mutual action between two people, so it must be used with と, not に.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: It becomes the causative form, meaning 'to make or force one's younger sister to marry,' rather than Tanaka marrying his younger sister.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q1.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners often translate it as 'marry someone' and mistakenly use を or に instead of the correct particle と.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vi: Excuse me, could you tell me how I can get to the station?
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: A polite opening phrase used before asking someone for help.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The destination particle に combines with は to emphasize the place the speaker wants directions to as the topic.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: An interrogative word asking about the method or way of doing an action.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb is changed to the past form and combined with ら to create a conditional form in a question asking for advice.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: A polite pattern for asking someone's opinion and requesting directions or advice.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.why: The structure 'Vたらいいでしょうか', combined with the question word 'どう', is a polite way to ask for directions and advice. The particle 'には' makes the destination the main topic so that the other person can give directions.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It is grammatically correct but has a more ordinary and slightly less formal tone than でしょうか.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: It has a rigid sense of obligation ('how one must go'), so it is less natural than たらいい when asking for directions.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.tip: Remember to change the verb to the past form た before combining it with ら. A common mistake is to attach it directly to the dictionary form, such as 行くたら.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q2.kobun.cn: Vたら ＋ いいですか / いいでしょうか
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vi: Mandarins are cheap, tasty, and also nutritious.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes mandarins the main topic for describing their features.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending in い changes to the て form to link qualities that are listed in the same direction with the following part.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The linking particle し follows the plain form to list advantages or reasons.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle も replaces が to add another positive point about the subject.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The predicate verb shows the existence of the quality and nutrients.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.why: This coordinated sentence uses the て form to connect adjectives and the linking particle し to list several notable advantages of mandarins. The particle も in the final part naturally creates an accumulating effect of positive points.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If we use only the linking sequence て, the sentence is still grammatically correct, but it does not highlight the impressive listing of reasons or advantages as clearly as し.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: It changes the meaning into a definite cause-and-effect relationship ('because it is tasty, it is nutritious'), which distorts the parallel listing in the original sentence.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.tip: When using し with an adjective ending in な or with a noun in the affirmative present tense, learners often forget to add だ. Correct examples are: べんりだし and すきだし.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな(だ)・N(だ) ＋ し
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vi: Because it was so hot, I accidentally fell asleep with the air conditioner left on.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The adjective ending in い changes to the て form to state the reason for the action in the following part.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action of turning on the device.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern たまま shows that the next action is performed while keeping the device switched on.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The main verb changes to the て form to connect with the auxiliary verb expressing an unintended result.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The structure てしまう expresses regret about an unintended action that has already happened.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.why: The pattern 'Vた＋まま' describes the speaker going to sleep while leaving the air conditioner switched on. The sentence ending 'てしまいました' emphasizes the carelessness and regret of falling asleep without turning it off.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: The meaning is incorrect because ながら refers to two active actions happening at the same time ('turning it on while sleeping'), whereas まま means maintaining an existing state.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: It simply describes two actions in sequence ('turn it on and then go to sleep') and does not emphasize the unintended continued state as まま does.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.tip: The verb before まま must be changed to the past form Vた in the affirmative. The dictionary form Vる must never be used.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q4.kobun.cn: Vた・Vない・Nの ＋ まま
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vi: When it comes to sports, Yamada is good at every event.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は introduces the person being discussed throughout the sentence.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern なら follows a noun to limit the scope of the topic being discussed.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The question word 何 combines with でも to mean the complete affirmative idea 'anything and everything.'
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending in な serves as the main predicate and expresses skill.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.why: The sentence places the topic 「山田さんは」 at the beginning, then uses 「スポーツなら」 to narrow the evaluation to sports, and combines 「何でも」 with the predicate 「じょうずです」 to state that the subject is capable in every area within that scope.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Using たら (スポーツだったら) gives a time-based hypothetical meaning, so it is less natural than なら when introducing a noun as a limited topic.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: It means 'something' (an unspecified event or sport), so it loses the complete praise 'good at every event' expressed by 何でも.
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse 「何でも」 ('anything and everything'—used with an affirmative sentence) and 「何も」 ('there is absolutely nothing'—which must be used with a negative sentence).
default.q.goukaku2_n4-t7-q5.kobun.cn: N・V普通形・Aい・Aな ＋ なら
